items.name: Rooftop solar PV, commercial (100 kW–1 MW, host-owned, installed)

cost.method: Lazard 2024 Community & C&I PV capital cost $1,300–2,900/kW (e2); LBNL Tracking the Sun 2024 state medians for 2023 installs: large (>=100 kW) non-residential $1.8–2.6/W, small non-residential $2.6–4.1/W (e1). Mid $2,300/kW = midpoint of Lazard range (~$2,100) nudged toward LBNL large non-residential state-median midpoint (~$2,200) plus a small rooftop premium because ~46% of LBNL large non-res systems are ground-mounted. Low $1,500 = just above Lazard low (large flat roofs, >500 kW); high $3,300 = within LBNL small non-res band (<100 kW or complex roofs). LBNL dollars are 2023 real; gap to 2024 is 1 year, so the range is stated in 2024 dollars per rule 5.

items.notes: Unit = kWdc of PV nameplate. Turnkey EPC price before incentives (no ITC deducted). Excludes roof replacement/structural reinforcement and utility interconnection upgrades (use utility-interconnection for large systems). Tax-exempt owners (schools, government) pay notably more in LBNL data.

items.name: Solar carport / parking canopy PV (steel canopy + PV, installed)

cost.method: GreenLancer 2026 planning range $2.75–3.50/W for larger commercial carports, $3.75–4.50+/W for smaller jobs (e3, low confidence). Mid $3,200/kW = upper-middle of the large-project band, cross-checked as rooftop mid ($2,300, e1/e2) + ~$900/kW canopy structure and foundations premium. Low $2,600 = large multi-row canopies; high $4,300 = small/complex jobs per e3.

items.notes: Unit = kWdc. Includes canopy steel, foundations (drilled piers), PV modules, inverters, under-canopy lighting typically excluded. Excludes parking-lot repaving, utility upgrades, and EV chargers. Replaces surface-parking shade structure cost where both would be built.

items.name: EV charger, Level 2 networked (per port, all-in incl. make-ready)

cost.method: Atlas EV Hub sample of utility program progress reports (2021): average ~$8,000 per L2 port including utility- and customer-side make-ready and hardware; California non-residential average $15,453/port; ICCT estimate ~$6,000/port (e4). PSEG Long Island 2022 make-ready alone $8,650/port (e5), which supports a mid above $8,000 once hardware is added. Mid $9,000 = Atlas average rounded up toward e5; low = ICCT; high = California average rounded.

items.notes: All-in per port: networked dual-port pedestal share, conduit/wire, panel capacity, trenching, utility-side make-ready. Costs fall per port as more ports are clustered at one site. Do not also add ev-make-ready for the same port.

items.name: EV DC fast charger, 150 kW class (per port, all-in)

cost.method: Evidence: utility programs averaged ~$115,000 per DCFC charger in 2021 (e4); PSEG Long Island make-ready alone $77,555 (community) to $116,330 (corridor) per port in 2022, before charger hardware (e5); Colorado NEVI total project cost $183,116–192,614 per port as of Oct 2024 (e6). Evidence spans 2021–2024 (>1 year), so the range is anchored on the 2024 NEVI data: mid $150,000 = between the 2021 utility average and the 2024 NEVI corridor figure (NEVI sites carry 4-port minimums, high-power 150 kW+ and corridor make-ready, so a non-NEVI commercial site sits below them). High $250,000 = corridor sites with transformer/service upgrades; low $100,000 = sites with existing capacity.

items.notes: Per port (one vehicle at a time). Includes charger hardware, installation, switchgear/transformer share and utility make-ready. Excludes land, canopy, amenities and ongoing network fees. Utility transformer upgrades are the main source of spread.

items.name: EV make-ready / EV-capable space (conduit, wire, panel capacity; no charger)

cost.method: PSEG Long Island 2022 implementation plan Level 2 make-ready per port: utility-side $5,000 + customer-side $3,650 = $8,650 (e5). A building-code 'EV-ready' space in new construction normally needs only the customer-side portion with a shared service, so mid $4,000 ≈ e5 customer-side $3,650 rounded up for panel/raceway capacity; low $2,500 = conduit-only EV-capable space in new construction (judgment, verify); high = full e5 utility + customer make-ready. Region left US although e5 is NY (higher-cost market) — treat high as NY-type.

items.notes: Use for code-required EV-ready/EV-capable parking spaces where the developer does not install chargers. Do not stack with ev-l2-port on the same space.

items.name: Battery energy storage, commercial & industrial (behind-the-meter, ~1 MW / 2 MWh)

cost.method: Lazard LCOS v9.0 (June 2024) C&I Standalone 1 MW / 2 MWh key assumptions (e7): initial capital cost DC $318–430/kWh + AC $45–80/kW (= $22.5–40/kWh at 2-hour duration) + EPC $59–159/kWh. Sum low = 318+22.5+59 ≈ $400/kWh; high = 430+40+159 ≈ $629/kWh; mid $500 = midpoint rounded.

items.notes: Unit = usable kWh. Installed LFP/Li-ion system incl. PCS and EPC; excludes utility interconnection upgrades and augmentation. Smaller (<100 kWh) systems run materially higher per kWh; 4-hour systems lower.

items.name: Utility interconnection and network upgrades (generation / storage)

cost.method: Berkeley Lab interconnection cost studies as reported: MISO complete projects averaged $102/kW (2019–2021) and recent storage $248/kW, solar $209/kW (e8); PJM complete projects median $30/kW, mean $84/kW (e9). $/kW × 1,000 = $/MW. Low = PJM median complete ($30k/MW); mid = MISO complete average (~$100k/MW); high = MISO storage average (~$250k/MW). Active/withdrawn queue projects ran far higher (PJM active mean $240/kW), so treat high as a non-extreme case.

items.notes: Transmission-queue interconnection (POI substation + network upgrades) for utility-scale solar, storage or wind, per MW of injection capacity. Behind-the-meter commercial systems usually face distribution-level studies and smaller fixed costs — do not apply per MW to small rooftop systems. Highly site- and queue-specific; verify with a utility study.
